blocks.c: John Wick - 2014 (2)

blocks.x: In 2014, after a number of flops, Keanu Reeves revived his career with the epic action-thriller John Wick. The film's simple premise —Reeves' eponymous retired hitman is grieving his beloved wife (Bridget Moynahan), when his treasured Ford Mustang is stolen and the son of a Russian mob boss kills the puppy, leading him on a bloody path of vengeance — didn't necessarily suggest the massive international blockbuster the franchise would become. But the film itself does, particularly in a single line in which Wick finally declares that he's "back." It's time to unpack one of the greatest lines in action movie history.

In John Wick, the titular character is a former underworld assassin who leaves his violent life behind to be with his wife, Helen. Before her death from cancer, Helen arranged for John to get a puppy to help cope with his grief. However, a group of Russian gangsters, led by Iosef (Alfie Allen), break into Wick's home, kill his dog, and steal his Ford Mustang. Having lost his wife and dog, John takes up his weapons once more and embarks on a blood-soaked path to hunt down Iosef, who is also the son of New York City's Russian mafia king, Viggo (Michael Nyqvist).

blocks.c: instar52549344.jpg

blocks.x: Later in the movie, Viggo and his men capture and tie up John, setting up an opportunity for the main villain and protagonist to confront one another. Wick is undeterred and wants revenge on Viggo's son. Viggo bemoans that "It was just a car! It was just a dog!" In an emotionally poetic monologue, Wick finally explains the significance of what Iosef took from him. The dog that Helen gifted to John was a "semblance of hope" and "an opportunity to grieve unalone." John angrily declares, "Your son took that from me! Stole that from me! Killed that from me! People keep asking if I'm back, and I haven't really had an answer, but yeah, I'm thinking I'm back! So you can either hand over your son or you can die screaming alongside him!" It's easily one of the most memorable and impactful moments in the movie.

blocks.x: Wick's monologue and the "I'm back" line encapsulate the entire movie. Through fate and circumstances, the world's most dangerous killer is unwittingly drawn back to the life he left behind. John Wick is a man who has lost everything and decides to pursue revenge against Iosef and anyone who stands in his way, including Viggo.

The scene is incredibly memorable because Wick is a fairly stoic character. He rarely shows such strong displays of emotion or palpable anger, and his righteous fury demonstrates how deeply this situation has affected him. It's also an emotionally raw and gut-wrenching scene as John drops his usually calm demeanor, showing his pure rage. Wick is a legendary hitman, or the "Baba Yaga," as he's nicknamed by the underworld. However, underneath that is a real human being who is in pain and suffering from his losses, and he's lashing out in the only way he knows how.
John Wick's Return Mirrors Keanu Reeves Career

blocks.c: John Wick - 2014 (1)

blocks.x: John Wick's famous line is interesting because it also holds a metatextual context. It's not just Wick who is "back" in business, but Keanu Reeves as well. John Wick proved to be a major turning point in Reeves' career. His stardom had been on the downward swing in previous years, and he was coming off the massively maligned flop 47 Ronin. John Wick was essentially the start of his comeback, or as many fans dubbed it, the "Keanu-ssance."

Although the first movie was only a modest success at the box office, grossing $43 million domestically and $86 million worldwide, John Wick was beloved by critics and audiences alike. It became a starting point for a new blockbuster franchise for Reeves, with each installment more successful than the previous one. John Wick made Reeves a bona fide box office success again and served as the precursor for his return to some of his iconic roles, including Ted Logan in Bill & Ted Face the Music and Neo in The Matrix Resurrections. Reeves also joined Pixar's iconic Toy Story franchise, voicing Duke Caboom in Toy Story 4 in 2019 and Toy Story 5 earlier this year.

The famous line signaled that Reeves was officially back as a cinematic action icon, and moviegoers are all the better for it. Currently, Lionsgate has multiple new editions of the John Wick franchise in the works, including John Wick: Chapter 5, with both Reeves and director Chad Stahelski attached to return. Moreover, Donnie Yen has been announced to direct and star in a new spin-off of the franchise focused on his character, Caine. John Wick: Chapter 4 felt like a proper endpoint for the character, so if Wick does return, hopefully a strong story accompanies it.

Nevertheless, Wick's incredibly quotable, classic line proves to be one of the movie's best moments and stands out as a career highlight for Reeves as well. The line definitely belongs in any career retrospective for the beloved actor.
